topics.title: Science by numbers
topics.intro: Scientists use percentages, ratios and rates all the time: how much oxygen is in the air, how to mix a solution, how fast something cools.
topics.teach: Explain how you would mix squash and water in the ratio 1 : 4.
topics.talk: Ask her how many litres of the air in a 500-litre space would be oxygen (21% of 500).
topics.hook: Per cent means out of 100; a ratio is a recipe, like 1 : 4 squash to water.

topics.title: Science words: spelling and meaning
topics.intro: Science words are built from Greek and Latin parts. Knowing the parts helps you spell them and work out what they mean.
topics.teach: Pick a science word and explain what each part of it means.
topics.talk: Ask her what “photo” means in photosynthesis and photograph.
topics.hook: Science words are built like Lego: **photo** (light) + **synthesis** (putting together).

visual.caption: Science words are built from Greek and Latin parts.

items.sentence: Green plants make their food by ___.
items.clue: how plants make glucose using light
items.explain: photo (light) + synthesis (putting together). The “f” sound is spelt ph.
items.learn: **photosynthesis**: photo (light) + synthesis (putting together). The “f” sound is spelt ph.
items.hook: Photo (light) + synthesis (making): plants make their food with light.

items.sentence: Every living cell releases energy by ___.
items.explain: re + spir (breathe) + ation: it is “spir”, not “sper”.
items.learn: **respiration**: re + spir (breathe) + ation: it is “spir”, not “sper”.
items.hook: re + SPIR + ation: think of “spirit”, the breath of life.

items.sentence: Leaves are green because they contain ___.
items.clue: the green substance that absorbs light
items.explain: chloro (green, with a hard “ch” as in chorus) + phyll (leaf): ph and a double l.
items.learn: **chlorophyll**: chloro (green, with a hard “ch” as in chorus) + phyll (leaf): ph and a double l.
items.hook: Chloro (green) + phyll (leaf): the green stuff in leaves.

items.sentence: My ___ is that sugar dissolves faster in warm water.
items.clue: an idea that can be tested
items.explain: hypo + thesis: y not i, then th in the middle.
items.learn: **hypothesis**: hypo + thesis: y not i, then th in the middle.
items.hook: A hypothesis is a hunch you can test.

items.sentence: Puddles disappear on a sunny day because of ___.
items.clue: a liquid turning into a gas
items.explain: e + vapor + ation: “vapour” loses its u here.
items.learn: **evaporation**: e + vapor + ation: “vapour” loses its u here.
items.hook: Water vanishes as vapour: e + vapour (drop the u) + ation.
items.example: Washing dries on the line by evaporation, fastest on warm, windy days.

items.sentence: The water droplets on a cold window are called ___.
items.clue: a gas turning back into a liquid
items.explain: con + dense + ation: drop the e from dense.
items.learn: **condensation**: con + dense + ation: drop the e from dense.
items.hook: con + dense (drop the e) + ation: vapour gets dense and turns to drops.
items.example: The steamy bathroom mirror after a shower is condensation.

items.sentence: Put the ___ away carefully after the experiment.
items.clue: the equipment used in an experiment

items.sentence: The ___ variable is the one you change.
items.hook: There’s a dent in indepen**dent**: it ends -ent, not -ant.

items.example: Doctors use a thermometer to check for a fever: about 37°C is normal.

items.sentence: The ___ controls what happens in a cell.
items.clue: the control centre of a cell
items.hook: The nucleus is the cell’s control centre: nu-CLE-us.

items.explain: Photo = light, as in photograph (“light drawing”).
items.hook: Photo = light: a photograph is a “light drawing”.
items.example: Solar panels on roofs are photovoltaic: they turn light into electricity.

items.explain: Chlorine gas is a pale yellow-green. Chlorophyll is the green in leaves.
items.hook: Chloro = green: chlorophyll makes leaves green.
items.example: Swimming-pool chlorine is named after the yellow-green colour of chlorine gas.

items.explain: Therm = heat. A thermal store is energy stored as heat.
items.hook: Therm = heat: a thermal flask keeps the heat in your hot chocolate.
items.example: The thermostat on the wall at home controls the heating: therm (heat) + stat (stay).
